chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from one of his companions, from Malik ibn Husayn al-Sakuni, who said:
Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'There is no servant who suppresses his anger except that Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, increases him with honor in this world and the Hereafter.'
And those who restrain their anger and pardon the people; and Allah loves the doers of good.
And Allah rewards him in place of that anger.
ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual reward for suppressing anger according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this hadith from al-Kafi, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) links the spiritual discipline of kanzm al-ghaydh (suppressing anger) to divine honor (izz), emphasizing that Allah replaces the feeling of humiliation or loss with elevated status in both worlds. This teaching is grounded in the Quranic description of the righteous as 'those who restrain anger and pardon people,' highlighting that self-control is not merely emotional regulation but a path to divine love and tangible reward. The narration underscores the Shia ethical ideal where inner tranquility translates into external dignity, reflecting the broader theological concept of divine recompense for moral excellence.
